subject: Geopolitics
title: Pipeline Politics
description: A micro-lesson that makes Pipeline Politics usable.

hook.text: Nord Stream 2, a $11 billion pipeline from Russia to Germany, was finished but never opened. Energy met politics.

buildup.text: Pipelines are fixed routes. Once built, supplier and buyer are locked together for decades. That lock creates power.

discovery.text: Transit countries charge fees and gain leverage. Ukraine earned $2 billion yearly from Russian gas passing through it.

twist.text: Russia built Nord Stream to bypass Ukraine entirely. Removing the middleman was both commercial and strategic.

climax.text: Every pipeline is a political statement. Routes are chosen not just for efficiency but for who they empower or bypass.

punchline.text: A pipeline is a permanent foreign policy decision in steel.

quiz.question: Why are pipelines geopolitically significant?
options: They are the cheapest way to transport any commodity
They lock suppliers and buyers into long-term dependencies
They can only cross friendly nations
